newsitem.title: USA: Assault charge follows airplane diaper dispute.
newsitem.headline: Assault charge follows airplane diaper dispute.

text.p: A Kansas City man pleaded not guilty in federal court on Wednesday to a charge he assaulted a woman passenger after she used the first-class lavatory on an airline to change her baby's diaper.

A lawyer entered the plea on behalf of Thomas Black, who was not in court for his arraignment on a misdemeanor charge of assault aboard an aircraft. If convicted, he could be sentenced to six months in prison.

Federal prosecutors said Black began kicking the door five minutes after Angela Thomas went into the first-class lavatory. An affidavit said Black told Thomas: "You should be using the bathroom in coach, where you paid. You don't belong up here."
Prosecutors also allege that Black slapped Thomas' face and used a racial slur.
"If he did anything, it was in self-defence," Black's lawyer, Brant Ladd, told reporters after the hearing. "We don't have any reason to think we will not prevail at his trial."

Ladd said Black denied the charges and had passed a polygraph examination. Black says he was struck and cut on the face in the incident, which occurred on a Delta Air Lines flight from Kansas City to Atlanta on April 4.
"She slapped him about the face. She has long fingernails," Ladd said.
